name: Samarra Archaeological City
description: Samarra was an Abbasid capital on both banks of the Tigris, about 130 km north of Baghdad, and its ruins stretch roughly 41.5 km along the river. For a century it governed an empire reaching from Tunisia to Central Asia. Its star sight is the 9th-century Great Mosque with its spiral minaret, and about 80% of the city remains unexcavated.
